correctness.rationale: The q-ary transfer preserves the binary exponent. Equality of two length-k windows has probability q^{-k} even with overlap, giving the same constant-density k-unique family. In the local edit bubble, binary complementarity is stronger than needed: the path-separation argument only requires each boundary symbol to differ from the edited symbol. For an alignment with d insertions, the record count gains q^d. In a bounded witness with R rules, the extra alphabet data consist of only O_t(R) symbols (edited symbols, boundary choices, and transfer labels), hence contribute q^{O_t(R)}, not an n-dependent positional exponent. Taking Q of size q^{A_t} n^{2t-1} polylog(n) absorbs those factors. The random integer-spectrum hash and rational-dependence extraction do not depend on the ambient number q^L of spectrum coordinates.

originality.rationale: The motivating En Gad preprint is still publicly indexed as v1 and proves the 2t-1 coefficient only for binary deletion codes. Targeted current searches for ordinary q-ary/nonbinary adversarial t-deletion codes with the same coefficient found burst-deletion and read-channel models, plus explicit nonbinary two-deletion constructions with larger redundancy, but no theorem covering this ordinary q-ary extension. The novelty claim is correctly confined to the alphabet transfer and uniform O_t(log q) bit overhead.

scientific_value.rationale: The result resolves a natural alphabet-extension question for a sharp new existential bound and shows that the factor-of-n improvement is not a binary-complement artifact. For fixed q and t=2 it lowers the existential leading bit-redundancy coefficient to 3, while remaining explicit about its nonconstructive nature.

citations.note: En Gad binary 2t-1 theorem; current public version indexed as v1.
Song–Cai nonbinary two-deletion construction with larger leading redundancy.
q-ary l-symbol read-channel deletion codes; different channel model.
q-ary burst-deletion codes; different burst model.

findings: The overlap-count identity q^s/q^{k+s}=q^{-k} is exact for every shift, including overlapping windows.
The q-ary local-bubble proof needs only left≠d and right≠d; the two boundary symbols need not coincide.
All additional alphabet choices in an R-rule witness cost q^{O_t(R)}, which the q^{A_t R} part of Q^R absorbs.
Current searches did not find an ordinary q-ary t-deletion theorem with the same 2t-1 coefficient; nearby results concern burst deletions or read channels.
independent_checks: Read and reran conceptually the supplied finite verification: 42 overlap-count cases and 532 q-ary boundary choices, all PASS.
Recounted exceptional alignments as n^{2d}q^d and verified A_t≥t makes that term uniform in q.
Stress-tested whether q^L spectrum dimension enters collision probability or the witness exponent; it does not once labels are independently hashed and the witness support is bounded.
Compared against current nonbinary two-deletion, burst-deletion, and l-symbol-read literature to avoid model conflation.
limitations: The construction is existential/randomized and does not supply efficient encoding or decoding.
The originality claim is vulnerable to near-simultaneous work because the binary preprint is extremely recent.
The audit validates the asymptotic witness accounting, not an implementation of the full binary proof in q-ary software.
